# Lessons index (generated: do not edit; run build_graph.py)
104 active, 22 superseded, 297 links.

## plan
- [ask-only-what-defaults-miss](preferences/ask-only-what-defaults-miss.md) (preference): Ask one question set only for what the lessons and defaults.json do not already answer; always ask which facecam (or none) and where the clips will be posted; defaults are CPU render, captions off, static editorial title, hook on, 40-55 s.
- [comparison-video-type](preferences/comparison-video-type.md) (preference): Support a comparison profile: two videos of similar places (e.g. GTA Vice City vs GTA 6 clubs) in a top and bottom split with labels, synced timing, and the user's own commentary; footage comes from sources the user is allowed to use, never altered to dodge detection.
- [every-aspect-editable](preferences/every-aspect-editable.md) (preference): Each clip is driven by a clip.json whose fields (trim, hook, captions, zoom, facecam, layout, audio) the user can change by saying it; re-render on CPU from the source, never re-run the whole pipeline.
- [finalise-then-hand-over](preferences/finalise-then-hand-over.md) (preference): When the user says finalise, finish every open build item in order (animations, restructure, history clean, transcript job), prove each, push to main, then give a short guide for starting the skill in a fresh chat session (what to attach, what to set up, what to type); say plainly what is untested.
- [find-all-moments-as-40-55s-clips](preferences/find-all-moments-as-40-55s-clips.md) (preference): Given any stream link (YouTube; Twitch untested), find all the best moments of the whole stream and cut each one as its own 40-55 s clip with the whole story (setup, peak, aftermath); go shorter or longer only when the story truly ends earlier or needs more, and say so.
- [highlights-yt-video-type](preferences/highlights-yt-video-type.md) (preference): Support a highlights profile: a 5-6 minute 16:9 1920x1080 video for YouTube made of the best moments with snappy pacing and heavy editing (transitions, meme text, zoom punches, speed ramps, sound effects, animated titles), commentary required for YouTube's reused-content rule, built only when the user asks.
- [leverage-available-skills](preferences/leverage-available-skills.md) (preference): Before building a step, check the installed skills and use one when it does the job well (titles, descriptions, moment ideas, code review, skill tuning, site pages); record which skill each step uses, and add new skills later when they bring something better.
- [refine-do-not-regenerate](preferences/refine-do-not-regenerate.md) (preference): Once the user likes a set of clips, stop making new clips, variants and extra features unprompted; apply only the refinements they ask for, on those clips.
- [scope-freeze-v1-then-backlog](preferences/scope-freeze-v1-then-backlog.md) (preference): New ideas go to the backlog in the plan and are not built until v1 has passed the final check, unless the user says build it now; v1 is frozen after one fix round following the user's review of real clips on a phone.
- [skill-runs-on-sonnet](preferences/skill-runs-on-sonnet.md) (preference): Write the clips skill so a Sonnet session can run it end to end: Sonnet picks moments, writes hooks and decides edits; it spawns Haiku sub-agents for simple work (download, fetch, upload, push, reading logs, running a given render command); it asks an Opus agent only for hard judgement calls.
- [video-type-profiles-gaming-first](preferences/video-type-profiles-gaming-first.md) (preference): Treat each video type as its own profile with its own steps and defaults; the current focus is gaming streams and gameplay videos, so build and tune that profile first and add others (podcasts, talking head) later.
- [final-validation-fable-then-fix](rules/final-validation-fable-then-fix.md) (rule): When everything is built, run one Fable agent that only validates the plan, skill, scripts, docs and lessons (no video generation, no fixing); then have Sonnet or Haiku agents fix the gaps it lists by priority, and repeat the check once.
- [learn-first-then-plan](rules/learn-first-then-plan.md) (rule): Before generating a clip, run lessons/query.py for the stages the job touches, then tell the user the plan (moments, length, layout, captions, zoom targets, character).
- [limits-retry-then-tell-user](rules/limits-retry-then-tell-user.md) (rule): When a step hits a limit (quota, block, tool failure, missing data), retry up to 3-4 times with a sensible fix, then stop and tell the user plainly what failed and what the options are; never invent a workaround that lowers quality (bad CPU transcripts, lower resolution, skipped checks, guessed rules).
- [friend-brief-what-we-take](decisions/friend-brief-what-we-take.md) (decision): Adopt: platform safe zones (keep title, captions and facecam out of the bottom 20% and right 15%), -14 LUFS / -1 dBTP loudness, an upload export preset (source frame rate, higher bitrate), a strong first 3 seconds check, light dither on the blurred bars, a genre/profile field, MediaPipe/YuNet for the cam position. Optional only on request: kinetic captions, filler and silence cuts, pattern interrupts every 3-5 s, cold open, loop ending, vocal chain, sfx, colour grade, B-roll cards. Skip: paid services (TwelveLabs, Auphonic, Runway, Creatomate, Shotstack, turnkey clipping APIs), Remotion, DaVinci.

## download
- [long-mode-in-v1-vm-limits](preferences/long-mode-in-v1-vm-limits.md) (preference): Handle 5-6 hour videos in v1 with the long mode: never download the whole file; fetch metadata, captions and low-bitrate audio on Kaggle, find moments there, download only the chosen windows, transcribe only candidate windows on the Kaggle T4 (CPU fallback only where it works), and use GitHub only for small results; if the VM runs short of disk, memory or time, move that step to Kaggle.
- [age-restricted-stop](gotchas/age-restricted-stop.md) (gotcha): If the video is age-restricted, stop and ask the user for a file or another link; do not look for a bypass.
- [long-jobs-detach-and-register](gotchas/long-jobs-detach-and-register.md) (gotcha): Start every long wait (Kaggle fetch-windows, prepare, whisper) detached with setsid nohup and a log with an EXIT line; before leaving it, check after 15 minutes that the process is alive; if the kernel is COMPLETE but no EXIT line, fetch its output or re-run, never keep waiting.
- [youtube-blocks-vm](gotchas/youtube-blocks-vm.md) (gotcha): Download on a Kaggle CPU kernel (kaggle.py download), then fetch the result to the VM; never bypass a bot check and never use cookies.
- [source-4k-policy](decisions/source-4k-policy.md) (decision): Cap source downloads at 1080p by default (the 1080x1920 and 1920x1080 outputs show no extra detail from 4K except in zoom-ins); when the user asks for best quality or a 4K source, download 4K only for the chosen windows, expect slower renders, and say so.

## moments
- [clip-length-40-55](preferences/clip-length-40-55.md) (preference): Aim each clip at 40-55 s so the viewer sees the entire story of the moment (setup, peak, aftermath); go shorter or longer only when the story truly ends earlier or needs more, and say so.
- [quality-not-cringe](preferences/quality-not-cringe.md) (preference): Hooks and titles must be real lines from the clip; avoid hype-filler and gimmicks.
- [streams-english-or-hindi](preferences/streams-english-or-hindi.md) (preference): Expect English or Hindi/Hinglish streamers; detect the language first and use the matching transcript, reaction-word list and caption script (Roman letters for Hinglish).
- [complete-moment-in-clip](rules/complete-moment-in-clip.md) (rule): A clip must contain the whole moment (setup, peak, reaction) with natural start and end on sentence boundaries; never cut it mid-moment, and extend toward 60 s rather than trim the payoff.
- [never-skip-moments](rules/never-skip-moments.md) (rule): Rank every window of the video with several signals (heatmap, loudness, reaction words, speech density, external picks), cover every zone, look at frames of the top picks, and report the windows still NOT CUT.
- [captions-are-the-clock](gotchas/captions-are-the-clock.md) (gotcha): Take moment times from the YouTube captions (word times); Higgsfield timestamps drift later in the video and cover only ~19.5 min.
- [whisper-t4-large-v3-batched-below-captions](gotchas/whisper-t4-large-v3-batched-below-captions.md) (gotcha): Prefer YouTube captions. The Whisper default is large-v3, batched 8, VAD min silence 500 ms, chunk 20 s (66% exact / 77% fuzzy word match vs captions, measured 2026-11-15); it is still below captions, so use it only for a video with no captions, tell the user first, and ALWAYS pass --lang hi for Hindi (auto language can translate it into English); long_run.py refuses a Whisper run on a Hindi stream without --lang.
- [higgsfield](tools/higgsfield.md) (tool): Free video analysis covers the first ~19.5 min only; editing skills are paid (0 credits).
- [moment-finder](tools/moment-finder.md) (tool): Ranks 40-55 s windows (default --min 40 --max 55) from heatmap, loudness, reaction words and speech density; merges external picks.
- [opusclip](tools/opusclip.md) (tool): Not usable without credit (0 minutes on the trial); accepts a YouTube link plus a start/end range.
- [vidiq](tools/vidiq.md) (tool): Credits per use (clips 9/min, trim 1); good as a moment finder, not as a layout.
- [model-trials-2026-11-14](decisions/model-trials-2026-11-14.md) (decision): Do not wire in the YAMNet sound-event score or the trained highlight scorer yet, and do not transcribe Hindi with Whisper on the VM CPU: YouTube captions read best, CPU Whisper is slow and worse, the scorer needs 10-20 streams of data. Test the Hinglish Whisper fine-tune and large-v3 on the Kaggle GPU instead.
- [peakcut-and-reel-tools-decisions](decisions/peakcut-and-reel-tools-decisions.md) (decision): From PeakCut take its picker-prompt rules, its Roman-script converter (MIT, as fallback for words missing from our map) and the (LOUD) marks; add ffmpeg scdet boundary snapping and two-pass loudnorm; build the Kaggle transcript job on faster-whisper alone before trying WhisperX; skip Auto-Editor for gaming and skip Remotion.
- [visual-plus-transcript-moments](decisions/visual-plus-transcript-moments.md) (decision): Run visual_scan.py (2 fps energy + contact sheets) in parallel with find_moments, let a vision sub-agent (Haiku default, Sonnet on request) read the sheets, then merge_moments.py: both agree = top, a reviewer rejection with a concrete reason demotes (shown, never dropped), a visual-only window is added only at reviewer >= 7; no visual files or moments.visual=off leaves the transcript order exactly unchanged.

## render
- [output-preview-in-git-master-on-keep](preferences/output-preview-in-git-master-on-keep.md) (preference): Render every clip with output.preset=preview (30 fps, CRF 20, small, goes to git); render an upload master (source frame rate, CRF 16-17, 192 kbps audio, -14 LUFS / -1 dBTP, 1080x1920 vertical, 1920x1080 landscape, never upscaled) only for the clips the user keeps, and store it in a private Kaggle dataset outside git.
- [render-cpu-first](preferences/render-cpu-first.md) (preference): Do everything on the VM CPU; use Kaggle GPU only for GPU-only work (Whisper large-v3, local LLM, image-to-video).
- [voice-demo-feedback-subtle](preferences/voice-demo-feedback-subtle.md) (preference): Keep any added reaction voice quiet (clearly below the streamer's voice and the game peaks, never overpowering), use only 2-3 short lines per clip placed on real beats and never over the streamer's speech, and prefer her own in-sync reactions (face and voice from the same video) over a separate synthetic voice, because mismatched reactions and a loud voice look too AI.
- [voice-level-tweak-on-request](preferences/voice-level-tweak-on-request.md) (preference): Keep the facecam voice at its quiet default (15 dB under the stream) and commentary at commentary.level_db -7; change a level only when the user asks.
- [voiceover-human-like-not-user-voice](preferences/voiceover-human-like-not-user-voice.md) (preference): When a clip needs commentary, use a synthetic voice that sounds human, with natural pacing, pauses and breaths and no robotic or AI-ish delivery; the user does not record their own commentary. Pick the voice by listening tests, never clone a real person, write the script in a spoken style, and have the user approve script and voice each time.
- [commentary-quiet-slots-rare](gotchas/commentary-quiet-slots-rare.md) (gotcha): Place each commentary line at the lowest-cost slot (transcript word coverage plus a 100 ms level scan, after a sentence end or pause) and accept overlap with the streamer's speech, keeping the duck at 3 dB, rather than dropping the line or raising her voice.
- [highlights-preview-size-cap](gotchas/highlights-preview-size-cap.md) (gotcha): Render the highlights preview with a VBV cap from output.size_cap_mb (85) and x264 medium; plain CRF 21 is about 3.6 Mbps on this noisy 1080p gameplay (150 MB for 5.9 min), so quality goes into the upload master.
- [highlights-segment-cache-and-overlay-retry](gotchas/highlights-segment-cache-and-overlay-retry.md) (gotcha): Render each highlights segment once from the source into work/ (hash of spec, source, fps, neighbour transitions, overlays); retry a cancelled HyperFrames render 3 times, and never reuse an intermediate that was built with a skipped overlay.
- [loudnorm-aac-headroom](gotchas/loudnorm-aac-headroom.md) (gotcha): Run two-pass loudnorm with TP = audio.true_peak - 0.4 so the AAC-encoded file stays at or under the limit; measure the written file with ebur128 peak=true.
- [highlights-audio-limiter-after-loudnorm](tools/highlights-audio-limiter-after-loudnorm.md) (tool): Mix stream (ducked with the commentary duck_expr), the sfx track and her voice track BEFORE the two-pass loudnorm (-14 LUFS, TP aims -1.4), then add alimiter 0.6 dB under the true-peak target so the AAC file stays at or under -1.0 dBTP.
- [openshorts](tools/openshorts.md) (tool): Clip generator we wrap with run.py; no parameter for hook wording, effects or dubbing; plain cut is already 1080x1920 with the layout baked.
- [cpu-beat-gpu-showdown](decisions/cpu-beat-gpu-showdown.md) (decision): For one chosen moment the CPU path takes ~2.5 min; the Gemini GPU path took ~18 min and could not turn captions off.
- [highlights-commentary-lead-script-ducked](decisions/highlights-commentary-lead-script-ducked.md) (decision): Write highlights commentary as a script file the lead Claude session fills (0-2 English lines of 6-18 words per segment, at most one line per 25 s of video plus intro and outro, silence when the gist is thin), voice it with Kokoro af_heart, and mix it with her peak about 7 dB under the stream's loudest speech peaks (level_db -7, measured as L=R stereo) and the stream ducked 4 dB (hard cap 4, 0.2 s attack, 0.4 s release) only while a line plays.

## layout
- [animations-only-for-highlights](preferences/animations-only-for-highlights.md) (preference): Default clips get the static editorial title and no progress line or other animations; the animated title, ring, tag, burst and progress line are for highlight videos or when the user asks for them.
- [edit-effects-on-request](preferences/edit-effects-on-request.md) (preference): Offer a library of optional edit effects (animated transitions, meme-style text, freeze-zoom, speed ramp, shake, glitch, flash, emoji pops, reaction cutaway, sound effects); the runner proposes 0-3 per clip, the user approves, and every effect is an editable event in clip.json; use ffmpeg and HyperFrames, original or openly licensed sounds and fonts only.
- [facecam-lower-in-layout-c](preferences/facecam-lower-in-layout-c.md) (preference): Place the safe-c facecam at x 40, y 1250 (spans y 1250-1475): lower than the first version but always above the bottom 20% zone (y >= 1536).
- [gameplay-stays-whole](preferences/gameplay-stays-whole.md) (preference): Keep the whole game frame full-width in the middle of the 9:16 with blurred bars; never crop it tight or split it top/bottom.
- [layout-c-safe-zones](preferences/layout-c-safe-zones.md) (preference): Use layout C as the standard social layout: game picture shifted up about 200 px, a facecam about 300 px wide at the left above the bottom 20% zone, nothing important in the bottom 20% or right 15%; keep a layout without the facecam for destinations that do not want her.
- [gemini-auto-layout-cuts-stream](gotchas/gemini-auto-layout-cuts-stream.md) (gotcha): Do not use the Gemini auto layout for gameplay streams; it enlarges the streamer's face and cuts the stream so it is not visible; use the CPU full-frame layout.
- [vidiq-layout-cuts-gameplay](gotchas/vidiq-layout-cuts-gameplay.md) (gotcha): Use vidIQ only to find moments and trim the plain 16:9 (edit_media trim, 1 credit); do the vertical layout yourself.
- [webcam-layout-crops-game-cpu](gotchas/webcam-layout-crops-game-cpu.md) (gotcha): Do not force the webcam/split layout without Gemini's auto layout; it crops most of the game.
- [animations-off-by-default-how-to-turn-on](tools/animations-off-by-default-how-to-turn-on.md) (tool): New clips ship with hook.animation=none, animations.on=false, animations.progress_bar=false and no events; to add animations run edit_clip.py CLIP.json hook.animation=reveal animations.on=true animations.progress_bar=true --render, then add events only after the user agrees.

## captions
- [captions-minimal-low-hinglish](preferences/captions-minimal-low-hinglish.md) (preference): Captions, when asked for, are small, low in the bottom bar, 3 words at a time, in English or Roman-script Hinglish, never over the stream or the facecam.
- [captions-off-by-default](preferences/captions-off-by-default.md) (preference): Default to no captions; only add them when the user says so.
- [hook-editorial-serif-auto-contrast](preferences/hook-editorial-serif-auto-contrast.md) (preference): Draw the top title in the editorial style (Playfair Display serif, one key word in italics, no box, soft shadow) and keep it readable on bright or white backgrounds: measure the brightness behind the title over its whole duration and add a soft dark scrim (or switch to dark text) when it is bright.
- [captions-never-over-stream](rules/captions-never-over-stream.md) (rule): Captions must sit fully inside a free bar (default: the bottom bar, between the game picture and the facecam) and never overlap the game picture, the facecam or the hook; the engine must refuse or move a caption position that breaks this.
- [gpu-path-no-captions-switch](gotchas/gpu-path-no-captions-switch.md) (gotcha): run.py on Kaggle burns captions in; for a no-caption clip use the clips engine (captions are off by default there).
- [transcript-leading-space](gotchas/transcript-leading-space.md) (gotcha): OpenShorts words need a leading space (faster-whisper style) or the captions glue together.
- [hyperframes](tools/hyperframes.md) (tool): HTML+GSAP to video; exports transparent WebM for hook cards (25 s for 4 s).

## zoom
- [zoom-follow-what-is-pointed-at](preferences/zoom-follow-what-is-pointed-at.md) (preference): When he points at or refers to something (dekho, look, map), look at the frame and zoom briefly to that thing, not just to the map.
- [zoom-hold-while-discussed](preferences/zoom-hold-while-discussed.md) (preference): Keep the zoom on while the topic is being discussed (ease in, hold, ease out); a stretch of talk = hits closer than 4 s.
- [zoom-subtle-by-default](preferences/zoom-subtle-by-default.md) (preference): Auto punch-ins are at most ~7% and ease in/out; only a pointed-at target gets a stronger zoom.
- [ffmpeg-crop-in-w-fixed](gotchas/ffmpeg-crop-in-w-fixed.md) (gotcha): When scaling with eval=frame, write the scaled size into the crop expressions (1080*Z), not in_w/in_h.

## facecam
- [ask-facecam-with-without-both](preferences/ask-facecam-with-without-both.md) (preference): At the start of a clip job ask whether the clips need the streamer-girl facecam: with, without, or both; uploads to the clipping site do not need her, social posts may. A clip can have several named outputs from the same clip.json.
- [facecam-from-library-passive-default](preferences/facecam-from-library-passive-default.md) (preference): Use the AI-generated girl as the facecam, taking the video from the facecam library (default girl_watching_10s, a passive reaction); her own audio is dropped unless facecam.voice=low is asked for; stills and LTX loops are only fallbacks.
- [facecam-rounded-rect-safe-c-library](preferences/facecam-rounded-rect-safe-c-library.md) (preference): Show the facecam as a rounded-corner 4:3 rectangle (not a circle), 300 px wide, at x 40 y 1250 on the left above the bottom 20% zone (layout safe-c, position left-above-ui); take the video from the facecam library; the user can supply a new reaction video at any time and choose it per run; bottom-right is only the classic layout.
- [facecam-subtle-expression](preferences/facecam-subtle-expression.md) (preference): Prefer a simple smile and looking at the game over big reactions; if the supplied video has big reactions, use its calm part unless told otherwise.
- [facecam-voice-optional-quiet](preferences/facecam-voice-optional-quiet.md) (preference): Default facecam is a passive reaction with her audio dropped (facecam.voice=off); facecam.voice=low mixes her English library line once, about 15 dB under the stream's speech level, never ducking the stream, only when asked.
- [girl-speaks-english-only](preferences/girl-speaks-english-only.md) (preference): Our AI streamer girl speaks English: every reaction video, voice line and voice-over for her is in English, even when the stream is Hindi or Hinglish; no Hindi or Hinglish lines for her.
- [facecam-ai-generated-only](rules/facecam-ai-generated-only.md) (rule): Animate only fictional AI-generated characters (user confirmed) or people who gave consent; never a real person's face.
- [facecam-girl-calm-range](gotchas/facecam-girl-calm-range.md) (gotcha): For the calm look use facecam.use_seconds [0,1.2] of girl_gemini-app_10s.mp4; her surprised face starts at about 1.5 s.
- [gemini-free-key-limits](gotchas/gemini-free-key-limits.md) (gotcha): Free key: text works (moment picking); image generation returns 429 on all models and there are no Veo models. Use the Gemini app (user-made) for characters.
- [facecam-library-six-reactions](decisions/facecam-library-six-reactions.md) (decision): Use girl_watching_10s as the default calm facecam; surprise, impressed, hype and disbelief are usable; the laugh clip has no audible laugh (the patched version waits for the user's ear check); the clips come out 10 s or 20 s.

## publish
- [many-upload-destinations](preferences/many-upload-destinations.md) (preference): Treat each upload destination as a profile (name, facecam yes/no, title on/off, length limits, format, credit or watermark rules, post-text format) and render one named output per chosen destination from the same clip.json; never assume a site's rules, verify them from its own docs or ask the user.
- [new-clips-easy-to-find](preferences/new-clips-easy-to-find.md) (preference): Keep a generated LATEST.md at the repo root (newest clips first: date, stream, title, video link, post-kit link) and date-prefix stream folders, so the newest work is one tap away on GitHub.
- [post-kit-per-clip](preferences/post-kit-per-clip.md) (preference): Next to each clip keep a post kit: YouTube Shorts title, description and tags; Instagram caption and hashtags; a credit line for the source streamer; rights status. Titles are real lines or honest descriptions, checked for length.
- [checkpoint-every-step-finalise-squash-to-main](rules/checkpoint-every-step-finalise-squash-to-main.md) (rule): Every render step saves to GitHub at once: checkpoint.py (called by make_clips after each clip, edit_clip --render, render_highlights, long_run after every step) commits only safe files and pushes the CURRENT session branch ccr-*; autosave.sh also pushes that branch when the lead runs it (bash .claude/scripts/autosave.sh when the platform reminder appears and about every 10 minutes; the platform reminder hook does not call it by itself). Stream content reaches main ONLY through finalise.py --stream S --yes: one squashed commit (tree of the branch, parent origin/main, message 'clips: <stream>, <n> clips (final)'), so WIP re-render blobs never enter main. Non-stream files (.claude, lessons, README) go to main via finalise.py --sync-docs from autosave. Never force-push, never push HEAD:main for stream files.
- [finalise-to-main-then-delete-from-vm](rules/finalise-to-main-then-delete-from-vm.md) (rule): Final clips and docs go to GitHub main with finalise.py --stream streams/<s> --yes (one squashed fast-forward commit); work in progress lives on the session branch ccr-*; delete VM copies of sources and scratch afterwards; when asked for a file, fetch it from GitHub (the branch has every WIP version, main only the final one) and send it.
- [no-copyright-evasion](rules/no-copyright-evasion.md) (rule): Never edit footage to dodge copyright detection; keep rights.status per clip (private-test until permission or real commentary) and block export otherwise.
- [repo-keeps-only-current-work](rules/repo-keeps-only-current-work.md) (rule): Keep in the repo only the current skills, plans, lessons, shared assets and the clips the user is working on; remove old experiments, old clip sets and unused scripts (text notes worth keeping go to archive/), and strip old large files from git history (done on 2026-11-15: history rewritten, old large files are gone from main; previews stay in git, masters live outside git; anything removed is not recoverable from git).
- [repo-site-ready-structure](rules/repo-site-ready-structure.md) (rule): Keep everything that runs (skills, scripts, plans, fonts, facecam and animation assets) under .claude/ at the repo root; keep published content under streams/<stream-slug>/clips/<clip-id>/ with one folder per clip (clip.mp4, clip.json, poster.jpg, edit notes) and a generated streams/index.json manifest, so a website can render straight from the repo; stable lowercase slugs, no loose files.
- [rockstar-policy-non-commercial](gotchas/rockstar-policy-non-commercial.md) (gotcha): Tell the user that Rockstar's policy allows posting game footage only if you do not make money from it, that credit and 'no infringement intended' give no legal cover, that fair use is decided only by a court, and that the real route for a monetised channel is a licence request to Take-Two; mute game and trailer audio, keep claimed Shorts at 60 s or less, and never edit footage to dodge detection.
- [youtube-reused-content-needs-commentary](gotchas/youtube-reused-content-needs-commentary.md) (gotcha): Tell the user that YouTube reviews clips and reaction content under its reused-content policy, even with the original creator's permission, and can remove monetisation for the whole channel; clips with added commentary or a real narrative are safer than a bare stream cut, and the decision to post is the user's.
- [clean-keeps-stream-webcam](decisions/clean-keeps-stream-webcam.md) (decision): The clean destination has no AI girl facecam; the stream's own webcam stays as part of the whole picture; all else (title, captions, zooms) may be on and animations only when asked.
- [masters-outside-git](decisions/masters-outside-git.md) (decision): Keep the small preview of each clip in git and store the full-quality upload master outside git, by default in a private Kaggle dataset per stream (the manifest links to it), because GitHub rejects files over 100 MB and our tools cannot create GitHub releases; fetch a master on request.
- [site-rules-unknown-find-later](decisions/site-rules-unknown-find-later.md) (decision): Whop and other content-reward sites have no verified profile (verified:false); rules differ per campaign: find them when the user supplies a brief or link; until then use the clean profile and warn.

## infra
- [kaggle-gpu-where-it-works-no-quality-fallback](preferences/kaggle-gpu-where-it-works-no-quality-fallback.md) (preference): Use the Kaggle T4 for work it does better (Whisper, model inference over many frames, fine-tuning) and stay well inside 30 h per week; clip rendering stays on the VM CPU; when the GPU step fails retry up to 3 times, then tell the user, and use a CPU fallback only where it gives the same quality (never CPU Whisper for Hindi).
- [small-offline-trainable-models](preferences/small-offline-trainable-models.md) (preference): Look for better open offline models per stage and fine-tune or train small ones when useful, but keep each model and the total on disk small (about 2 GB per model, 5 GB in total) and delete unused model caches.
- [agents-never-see-kaggle-key](rules/agents-never-see-kaggle-key.md) (rule): Run Kaggle calls for any account through scripts/download/kaggle.py [--account 2] raw <cli args>; never read, print or copy a key or the kagglegpu2 PDF.
- [fable-orchestrates-only](rules/fable-orchestrates-only.md) (rule): The lead (Fable) plans, writes specs, checks results and commits; ALL execution (renders, edits, code, docs, tests) goes to Haiku or Sonnet sub-agents; an Opus agent may be used as an advisor sometimes; keep token use low.
- [keys-never-in-chat](rules/keys-never-in-chat.md) (rule): Keep API keys only in environment variables or Network secrets of the Claude environment; never print, paste, log, commit or ask for them in chat. A private Kaggle dataset is only a transfer copy: delete it once the keys are in the environment.
- [retro-step-9-and-incident-table](rules/retro-step-9-and-incident-table.md) (rule): End every clip job with step 9 (retro.py): each finding gets exactly one disposition (lesson, check, doc, backlog, or none with a reason); an incident in lessons/incidents.json with count >= 2 and enforced_by none becomes a preflight check before the next job starts, unless the user defers it.
- [tick-first-during-jobs](rules/tick-first-during-jobs.md) (rule): The first action of every turn while a job is open is python3 .claude/skills/clips/scripts/jobs.py tick; arm send_later at ETA + 10 minutes and re-arm it every 15 minutes (tick --wake counts them, 12 wakes at most per job); Monitor is only the fast path, /loop only when the user is watching live; never depend on ScheduleWakeup or CronCreate surviving a restart.
- [time-and-log-every-run](rules/time-and-log-every-run.md) (rule): Record UTC start/end of every step, keep an exact run log in docs/, and list the skill gaps found after each run.
- [classifier-blocks](gotchas/classifier-blocks.md) (gotcha): Bot-check circumvention, unauthorised token use and Kaggle deletes were denied; report it and do not retry the same call.
- [hyperframes-needs-disk](gotchas/hyperframes-needs-disk.md) (gotcha): Keep several GB free before rendering; delete finished scratch first. Transparent WebM export works for hook cards.
- [read-before-write-same-file](gotchas/read-before-write-same-file.md) (gotcha): Never write open(p,'w').write(f(open(p).read())): the write-open truncates first and the file ends up empty; read into a variable first.
- [kaggle-two-accounts](tools/kaggle-two-accounts.md) (tool): GPU kernels run on account 1 (ARVR7Plays); only a QUEUED-over-20-min or quota/GPU-hours failure moves the whole chain to account 2 (sovere); CPU jobs stay on account 1; never print the account-2 token.
- [kaggle](tools/kaggle.md) (tool): CPU kernel for downloads, T4 for GPU jobs, private dataset for keys; title must equal slug.
- [kokoro-commentary-tts-venv-312](tools/kokoro-commentary-tts-venv-312.md) (tool): Install Kokoro 0.9.4 in a python 3.12 venv (tts.py --setup: uv venv -p 3.12, torch CPU wheel, spaCy en_core_web_sm) and render with speed 0.85; never substitute another voice when it is missing, exit 3 with the install command.
